name: Heth
overview: Heth is a male figure identified as the son of Canaan and associated with the Hittite tribe. His mention in Scripture primarily establishes his role as a progenitor within the genealogical records of the descendants of Canaan. Beyond this, there are no additional personal notes or detailed accounts of his life.
namesAndTitles: The name Heth appears as a proper name in Genesis 10:15. No specific meaning or divine origin is attributed to the name in the biblical text, indicating it is simply a personal name without further explicated significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Heth as the son of Canaan. He is also considered an ancestor to several notable individuals, including Zohar, Ephron, Beeri, and Elon, linking him to key figures associated with the Hittite lineage. These relationships highlight his role in the broader family tree of the Canaanite peoples.
scriptureSignificance: Heth's significance lies in his position as a foundational ancestor of the Hittite tribe, a people frequently mentioned in the Old Testament. Through his lineage, important figures connected to biblical narratives emerge, underscoring the historical and genealogical framework of the descendants of Canaan. Thus, Heth serves as a critical link in understanding the ethnic and familial origins of the Hittites within God's providential plan recorded in Scripture.
